items.what: The lift template set is restated three times in transports(): LIFTS (line 25), the `sites` table (lines 129-137) and the fit selection here (UC templates 20649/20652/20655 and TB templates 4170/4171/47296/47297 on line 167). items.what: classicdb() has its own copy of gen_routes.download() (gen_routes.py:63-79): the cache check, the offline error, the same User-Agent and timeout, and the temp-file-then-replace write. gen_transit already imports download from gen_routes. Canonical home: gen_routes.download, with a binary/validator option.
items.why: Intended differences: classicdb keeps bytes (gzip) and checks them with gzip.decompress, while download decodes text and rejects HTML. Accidental drift: the temp name is built as path.with_suffix('.tmp') here but path.suffix + '.tmp' in download, and the User-Agent string is duplicated. A change to caching or headers (a new UA, retries, a different timeout) would have to be made in both.

items.quote: request = urllib.request.Request(DB_URL, headers={"User-Agent": "ShortestPathForever/1.0"})
items.what: classicdb() re-implements the cached-download routine of gen_routes.download() (tools/gen_routes.py:63-79): cache path under CACHE, refresh/offline switch, 'Missing cached source' error, the same User-Agent literal, urlopen with timeout 60, temp-file-then-replace. gen_transit already imports download from gen_routes; download is the canonical home (e.g. give it a binary/validate hook).
items.why: Differences: classicdb stores bytes and validates with gzip.decompress (download decodes UTF-8 and rejects HTML), and its temp suffix is '.tmp' instead of '<suffix>.tmp'. Both are intentional per-format validations that a validator parameter would keep; the rest (UA string, offline/refresh semantics, atomic write) is copied and would need any fix twice.
items.reason: The functions serve different format and return contracts: download() returns decoded UTF-8 text, while classicdb() retains compressed bytes and streams SQL into parsed tables. Passing the real cached gzip file through download() raises UnicodeDecodeError while classicdb() succeeds, supporting the lens's different-contract exception.

items.quote: # Sizes in UI units draw at that many units' worth of pixels at every UI scale, so they widen with the render
items.what: stale/contradictory: attributes UI-unit stroke sizes to Route.lua, which sizes them in physical pixels
items.why: Route.lua divides every thickness by the effective scale (Stroke: SetThickness((dot and owner.dot or THICKNESS) / scale), scale = GetEffectiveScale() in Line), so widths are fixed physical pixels; render_demo's own comment ('Route.lua fixes stroke widths in physical pixels') says the same. flush_strokes multiplies by the render scale k, so this comment should say the static PNGs deliberately widen strokes with the render scale (a mock choice), not that the addon draws them that way. Owner to confirm which is intended.
items.reason: The mock models effective scale 1 and separately magnifies its output through wowmock.Canvas.px; docs/screenshots.md explicitly distinguishes 2x static renders from the final-size GIF. An in-memory execution produced core/outline widths of 2/4 pixels at render scale 1 and 4/8 at scale 2, matching this comment's rendering contract.

items.quote:
map_id = 1432
    base, rects = map_base(ui, map_id)
items.what: render_stops (tools/screenshots.py:561-569) re-implements map_canvas's map-scene setup (tools/screenshots.py:397-405): copy the map_base frame into a fresh canvas, unpack rects["map"], make the route canvas, and a local point() that projects into map-rect units; both then flush_strokes the route, paste it at (mx, my) and call map_landmarks. Canonical home: a shared helper (e.g. map_layers(ui, map_id) returning canvas, rect, route, point) used by map_canvas and render_stops.
items.why: The jscpd 11-line clone is real, not coincidental: both copies express one fact, how a map screenshot is layered (frame copy, route overlay at the map rect in map-relative units, then landmarks), so a change to that layering (route canvas scale, paste offset, landmark order) must land in both. Differences: map_canvas's point() returns None for an unprojectable point while render_stops' point() assumes projection succeeds (fine for the fixed Loch Modan scene, but a missing assignment would surface as a TypeError rather than a skip); the rest is identical. Low stakes (dev tooling, output checked byte-for-byte by --verify), hence medium.
items.reason: The small-idiom exclusion applies: both renderers already share map_base, projection, flush_strokes and map_landmarks; the repeated code assembles their canvases. Their contracts differ: map_canvas tolerates unprojectable cross-map points and returns a full frame, while render_stops requires local projections, reserves stop-marker gaps and returns a cropped scene.

items.what: ns.NearbyServices (typed here, defined in Nearby.lua:276) is test-only. No runtime file reads it. tests/nearby_spec.lua reads only State, Index and Nearest. Build, Navigate and Services are read nowhere. Fate: test-only. Delete the export, or narrow it to what the spec needs.
items.why: `grep -rn NearbyServices` over the whole repository finds only Nearby.lua (its class and definition), tests/nearby_spec.lua and this field. `git grep NearbyServices` finds no hit on any of the six in-flight branches.
